title: Short term antibiotic therapy in Patients with cholangitis and complete biliary drainage: A prospective trial
summary:
Acute cholangitis is a bacterial infection of the biliary tract, which usually occurs in the course of incomplete biliary drainage. If there is no prompt therapy, cholangitis is potential life threatening. The therapy most often consists of interventional bile drainage via endoscopic retrograde cholangiography in combination with antibiotic treatment. Duration of the antibiotic treatment varies between 3 and 10 days. There is few high quality evidence concerning the optimal duration of the antibiotic treatment. Current data suggest that a 4 day course might be sufficient, if complete drainage is present. 
This study is designed to prospectively evaluate the guideline recommendations. The study takes place at the University Hospital Frankfurt.

interventions.name: Patients will be contacted after 4 weeks to exclude occurence or recurrent cholangitis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients with Diagnosis of Cholangitis I° and II° (Tokyo Guidelines 2018) and after ERCP with stent insertion and sufficient biliary drainage 
2. Antibiotic treatment according to Tokyo Guidelines 2018
Exclusion criteria:
1. Age <18J.
2. Already participated at this study
3. Insufficient biliary drainage
4. Septic patient (IMC-pflichtig, Cholangitis III°)
5. Concomittant acute biliary pancreatitis
6. Concomittant decompensated comorbidity
7. Concomittant infection of other etiology
8. Dialysis
9. Chemotherapy
10. Severe psychiatric disease
11. Gram positive bacteria in blood culture
12. Post liver transplant with purulent cholangitis in ERCP
